content.comment_body: I'm working for a contractor that uses [product_name] controllers in many of their products, but the provided editor software does not appear to support actual coding. While the flowchart-based graphical interface functions, I would prefer to write my own logic directly. Having worked with controllers in the past that supported C or Python (especially useful for Linux users), I find this limiting. I know [company_name] offers other products with command-line programming support, but [product_name] seems to be an exception. I would welcome any advice from the community.

analysis.insight_summary: The user highlights a gap between their preference for text-based programming languages such as C or Python and the flowchart-style graphical interface required by the [product_name] software editor. Compared to past experiences with more flexible PLC programming environments, the current editor for [product_name] is seen as restrictive and lacking options for advanced code development.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to have the option to program [product_name] controller logic with textual languages like C or Python, seeking greater flexibility in the interface, including command-line or code-based development methods.
